explanation: Sparse transcoder feature (nonzero on 2% of steps), active only at D1. Its magnitude is driven by the previous trial being a1 -> S1 (common) unrewarded: that indicator alone gives dev R^2 0.24 beyond timing. Within those D1 steps it is larger when the trial before was also unrewarded (+0.21), smaller later in the episode (-0.007 per trial), smaller when the trial before reached S1 (-0.10), and it grows with the size of the D1 policy lean in either direction (slope +0.17 on the a1 side, -0.11 on the a2 side, so roughly |choice|). Six terms, all observed or model-internal (no future variables): test R^2 beyond timing 0.589, which is above the profile all-cue additive ceiling of 0.38 because these are interaction terms. What it misses: some strong firing on runs of consecutive unrewarded D1s after a2 S1 u or at the start of the window. Adding terms for a2 S1 u, three-loss streaks, value or since_rev added under 0.01.

issues: The claim that the activation 'follows roughly |choice|' and 'grows with how strongly the D1 policy leans either way' is wrong. I binned D1 choice within last_is('a1 S1 u') on test and got these weights: choice<-2: -0.026, -2..-1: -0.023, -1..0: -0.028, 0..1: -0.013, 1..2: +0.042, 2..3: +0.142, >=3: +0.625. So the a2 side is flat and the activation rises only with a strong a1 lean. The -0.11 a2-side slope comes from fitting two clipped lines with a forced kink at 0. With a (choice>0) step term added, the a2-side slope drops to -0.0007.

The policy dependence is the second-biggest driver, not a modifier. Dropping the a2-side clip term cuts test R^2 from 0.589 to 0.430, and dropping the a1-side term cuts it to 0.501. A label that says 'strong policy lean' without a direction misdescribes it. The earlier firing label ('moderate a1 lean') and the D1 policy-decile residuals (deciles 1-5 at about -0.03, decile 8 at +0.073) both point to an a1 lean.

The explanation says extra a2 S1 u terms each added <0.01. That holds only for the plain indicator. (phase==D1)*last_is('a2 S1 u')*clip(choice,0) adds +0.027 on test (0.589 -> 0.616). The worst-fit windows in misses are mostly big D1 firing after a2 S1R unrewarded (actual 1.0-1.8, predicted about 0.06). So the feature is really 'S1 reached and unrewarded, while still leaning a1', not something specific to a1 S1 u.
Window-start D1s (previous trial unknown) with a strong a1 lean are a smaller unmodelled pocket. Adding (phase==D1)*(prev_action==-1)*clip(choice-2.5,0) adds about +0.007.

Claims that check out: active only at D1 (GO and D2 baseline and residuals are 0). Larger after a second loss (+0.19 to +0.21). Declines with ep_trial (-0.007 per trial). Smaller when the trial before that reached S1 (between -0.05 and -0.10, depending on the choice shape). No future variables are used. The magnitude of the score (0.589 test) is genuine.
